clauses.reason: The title and enacting words of EO 11092 state the order's subject, assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Federal Communications Commission, and the authority under which the President acted, including Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 and section 606 of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended (47 U.S.C. 606); they operate only through the numbered sections that follow, so they ended with the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 1 of EO 11092 directs the Federal Communications Commission, subject to the policy guidance of the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning, to prepare national emergency plans and develop preparedness programs covering provision of service by common carriers, broadcasting facilities and the safety and special radio services, assignment of radio frequencies to Commission licensees, and the protection, reduction of vulnerability, maintenance and restoration of facilities operated by its licensees in an emergency, designed to develop a state of readiness in those areas. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 2 of EO 11092 defines terms used in the order, beginning with common carrier and broadcasting facilities. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 3 of EO 11092 directs the Commission to develop plans and procedures, in consonance with national telecommunications plans and policies, covering common carrier service, broadcasting service, safety and special radio services, radio frequency assignment, electromagnetic radiation, investigation and enforcement, conservation, salvage and rehabilitation, and claimancy. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 4 of EO 11092 directs the Commission, in consonance with the national civil defense plans, programs and operations of the Department of Defense under Executive Order No. 10952, to provide facilities protection advice and guidance and to carry out damage assessment. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 5 of EO 11092 directs the Commission to foster or conduct research in areas directly concerned with the Commission's emergency preparedness responsibilities. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 6 of EO 11092 sets the guidance by which the Commission, in carrying out the functions assigned in the order, is to be guided: interagency cooperation (including plans in consonance with plans for mobilizing the Nation's telecommunications resources under Executive Order No. 10705, Executive Order No. 10995 and Executive Order No. 11051), Presidential coordination (the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning is to advise and assist the President in determining policy for the performance of functions under the order), and emergency planning (plans, programs and organization are to be developed as an integral part of the Commission's continuing activities, and the Commission is to be prepared to implement all appropriate plans developed under the order). It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 7 of EO 11092 provides that nothing in the order is to be construed as conferring authority under Title III of the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course of action prepared or developed pursuant to the order; the section ends there and does not reserve that authority to anyone. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 8 of EO 11092 authorizes the Commission to reassign, within the Commission and its staff, the functions assigned to it in the order. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 9 of EO 11092 provides that nothing in the order derogates from the provisions of Executive Order No. 10705, Executive Order No. 10995 or Executive Order No. 11051; that any order with respect to telecommunications issued under authority conferred by those orders, or by orders they revised or superseded, continues in full force and effect, except as inconsistent with this order, until amended, modified or terminated by appropriate authority; and that, to the extent of any inconsistency between any other prior Executive order and this order, this order controls. These were continuing provisions of this order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11092: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (19), "Executive Order No. 11092 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision. The wording in this section that continues the telecommunications orders until they are amended, modified or terminated by appropriate authority concerns those orders, not the term of EO 11092 itself.

research_rationale:
EO 11092 (1963-02-26; Assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Federal Communications Commission) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (28 FR 1847, Federal Register of 1963-02-28), whose file also contains neighbouring material; the order was delimited by its heading and the John F. Kennedy signature line. The dossier's machine segmentation, which cuts sections into lettered fragments and repeats some, was replaced by 10 scopes: one for the enacting words and one for each numbered section. Its own terms contain no end date or termination condition; the only "until" wording is in Sec. 9, about the telecommunications orders it continues. It ended on 1969-10-28 by express revocation in EO 11490, Sec. 3015, item (19), cited from the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 255823; page record checked: heading, date and text hash agree with the held text) and read for corroboration in the Federal Register print of 34 FR 17567 onward (OCR text), which lists the same order. No amendment, suspension or other instrument naming it is held besides EO 11490, which revokes it. The selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog) are coverage statements read before use; they are leads, not independent review.

savings.reason: Item (19) of Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 revokes EO 11092. In the held American Presidency Project transcription, Sec. 3014 reads: "Except as provided by Section 3015, nothing in this order shall be deemed to derogate from any now existing assignment of functions to any department or agency or officer thereof made by statute, Executive order, or Presidential directives, including Memoranda." Because Sec. 3014 begins with that exception, it does not preserve the revoked order. The end source span cited for this claim runs from "SECTION 501. Functions." through Sec. 3015, that is Parts 5 through 30 of EO 11490. I read Sec. 3014 and Sec. 3015; I did not read the other Parts to decide whether any of them carries this order's commands forward, so no transfer or accrual is claimed and the state is none_after_bounded_search.
